subject: Allow specify user to reset password

inline.message: this requires the guest to be deployed with the qemu guest agent correct. with out the guest agent i dont think libvirt can reset the password.
unfrotunetly yes although they should really be using ssh keys or x509 certs for powershell on windows.

vms are owned by the project so if we did this it would allow any memeber of a project to reset the password of any vm in the project. is that what we want? the most comment case other then forget the password where this would come up is an employee leave but they did nto transfer the vm to another and reset the password before they left.

this is the user in the vm.

this would only work if the vm supported local login by the way. i dont think we would expect this to work if the vm use kerberous or a windows domain login right?

see the issue with this is if that is a shared vm it would still  allow the non admin to reset the password of any user on the vm. that said i dont see a way to prevent that and still support letting the user reset there own accrount.

i think there are several security impacts to this.

as i said above vms are owned by projects not users so this api would presuable allow any user of the poject to reset an user in the vms password. that seam like a pretty big security whole if that vm is shared between users.

in a public cloud env i see a need to be able to disable this feature i also think its likely that users would want to be able to disable this feature rather then have it contoled by the operator. as such i think we would need a hw_user_resetable_password image metadata property or something similar to allow them to enable this feature if they want it but i think it should be disabled by default.

the alternitve would be to make this an admin only api by default with a new policy rule and allow operators to allow this via modifying the policy rule if the choose.

in either case i dont think we should enable this by default for all vms that have the qemu geust agent enabled.

subject: [NB] Add "if_exists" flag to ACL and Port_Group deletion commands

inline.message:
It seems a little confusing to have acl_del(if_exists=True) mean "Delete this ACL if the underlying port group or logical switch exists" as opposed to "delete this ACL if it exists".

I guess we can assume that if the port group or switch doesn't exist, the ACL also doesn't exist, and the existing behavior with respect to ACLs on these entities already behaves as if_exists were True (we don't raise an error if there is no match). But in the case of the new default value of if_exists=False, does that mean that if we go through the list of entity.acls and we don't match any ACLs that we *should* throw an error?

I'm open to this change, just checking to make sure we've covered everything. Regardless, `ovsdbapp/schema/ovn_northbound/api.py` needs to be updated to match the impl and have the behavior documented.

subject: Allow admin to specify project id on creation
body:
(2 comments)

This cannot be a "general use" part of the API imo. I'm going to stick by my concerns. I really want, if this is going to be implemented, it being an ADMIN only action [meaning in the system-scope kind of world, it is a cloud-admin action].

I think we have a lot of issues with this proposal outlined here:

What occurs when an ID is in conflict? UUID4 is effectively unique, but with this system it is possible that someone can squat on an ID or could select an ID that could be UUID (e.g., "deadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeef") and prevent folks from another cloud from consuming it.

I also do not want people to specify (and require sanitization of the input) the IDs. Keystone has long stated it controls the IDs internally, this is to prevent failures based upon input of data (if someone sets a non-UUID form ID).

-2 is for in-line comment regarding fernet across multiple non-replicated keystones. I am very much not comfortable with this from a security standpoint.

I'll walk back my -2 to a -1 once that goal/support is removed from the spec.

inline.message:
If the plan is to support (explicitly) the use of fernet issued from one keystone in another, I'm a hard -2 on this.

I can't stop folks from trying to implement this. This should not be an explicit goal. Each keystone should *always* be explicitly authoritative for it's own auth. IF you want this setup, use keystone-to-keystone. This is exposing large security risks between deployments. If the keystones are replicated/in sync, this is fine.

Realize this also requires keystone to have all identity data 100% in sync/identical - you cannot do this without supporting pretty much complete support of setting IDs on every resource in keystone (which I'm also a hard -2 on).
Names are also not globally unique. This means that users cannot rely on this without also relying on domain_name/domain_id.
